ATT&CK® Framework

MITRE ATT&CK® v19 · the Linux surface, resolved to analytics and data components

The published framework is the vocabulary everything else on this site is joined to. It arrives as a STIX bundle and is reduced here to the part that can be observed on Linux, then resolved the whole way down: a tactic holds techniques, a technique holds sub-techniques, each carries detection strategies, each strategy carries analytics, and an analytic names the data components it needs. Only the last of those is something a sensor can actually produce, which is why the chain is kept whole rather than flattened.

Every leaf of that chain gets an event key, and the key is the join. It carries the tactic, the technique and sub-technique, the analytic and the data component in one string, so a row of telemetry can be traced back to the published page it claims to detect — and so a claim with no data component behind it is visible as such. A second corpus maps the same techniques to Linux-targeting campaigns, which is what turns coverage into priority: what is documented, and what has actually been used.
